research.approach: Practitioners who bring a close down to about five days stop treating it as one month-end rush. They fix a calendar with cut-offs and named preparers and reviewers, reconcile cash and payment platforms early and continuously, run accruals and prepayments from a schedule with auto-reversing journals, reconcile the balance sheet from stable support, review accounts before every task is finished, and lock the period last. After each close they remove one root cause. In Xero the lock date and the Bank Reconciliation Summary are the final gates.

steps.name: Time today's close and find the critical path
steps.why: The longest chain of dependent tasks sets the close length; speeding up other tasks changes nothing.

steps.name: Fix a close calendar with cut-offs, owners and backups
steps.why: A standard calendar with day targets and escalation stops the team renegotiating dates each month.

steps.name: Reconcile bank, card and Stripe accounts early and continuously
steps.why: Cash is the first integrity check and pile-ups here delay everything after it.

steps.name: Reconcile inventory, receivables, payables and suspense
steps.why: Balance sheet accounts must tie to their support, with differences explained and nothing left in suspense.

steps.name: Run accruals and prepayments from one schedule
steps.why: Xero has no native schedule, so the schedule must tie to the ledger and accruals should reverse automatically.

steps.name: Review statements against last month and budget before sign-off
steps.why: Early account-level review finds issues while they are small and gives each big movement an explanation.

steps.name: Sign off, post approved entries and lock the period
steps.why: Without a lock date, entries can be back-dated into the closed month and published reports stop matching the ledger.

steps.name: Hold a short retrospective and remove one root cause a month
steps.why: Tracking late accounts and late inputs turns each close into a faster one.

pitfalls.text: Skipping the lock date, so entries are back-dated into closed periods and published reports stop matching the ledger.
Overlapping CSV imports and live bank feeds create duplicate bank lines.
Items left in suspense get harder to trace the longer they sit.
Expenses or revenue recorded in the wrong period, or accruals and prepayments not reviewed against prior months.
Late review creates rework; a close whose length varies each month erodes confidence in the numbers.

plan.name: Close the month in five working days

stages.name: Pin down the problem
stages.goal: Turn the owner's words into a measured close problem, target, limits and the data we can reach. Writes BRIEF.md.

stages.name: Time the current close and pull the ledger state
stages.goal: Collect the last close's task timings from the team and the account state from Xero, so the baseline is measured and not just reported.

checks.name: Every task from the last close has an owner and start and finish day, or is marked unknown
Account balances in the notes match the Xero trial balance for the same date
The measured close length is stated next to the owner's estimate of 15 days

stages.name: Check the books are ready to close
stages.goal: Find what is unreconciled and why: unreconciled bank and card lines by age, the Stripe clearing balance, duplicate bank lines, suspense balances and the lock date.

checks.name: Each of the three bank accounts and the Stripe clearing account has a ledger balance, a statement balance, the gap and the count and age of open items
Overlapping imports and feed lines are checked for duplicates
Suspense and unidentified balances are listed with age
Ends with CHECKED, LIMITED or UNRELIABLE and what that means for the diagnosis

stages.name: Find what sets the close length
stages.goal: Build the critical path from the timings and test each hypothesis against the evidence; keep competing explanations.

checks.name: The longest chain of dependent tasks is named with days per task
Every hypothesis is marked SUPPORTED, REFUTED or UNKNOWN with evidence
Findings that rest on owner-reported numbers are labelled as reports

stages.name: Rank the changes that cut days
stages.goal: Turn supported findings into ranked changes, each with the days it should save, effort, risk and how it will be measured.

checks.name: Every option cites the finding it rests on
Every option has days saved, effort, risk and how it will be measured
Total effort fits a two-person team

stages.name: Finance manager and owner choose
stages.goal: The finance manager and owner pick the changes to make. Ask why when the top option is passed over and record it.

checks.name: Chosen and passed-over options are recorded with reasons

stages.name: Write the close calendar and checklist
stages.goal: Build the dated close calendar with cut-offs, preparer, reviewer and backup for each task, day targets and an escalation path for late inputs.

checks.name: The calendar reaches sign-off by working day 5 and the critical path fits it
Every task has a preparer, a reviewer and a backup, and no one person is overloaded
Cut-off dates for sales, bills and payroll are written down

stages.name: Catch up and standardise reconciliations
stages.goal: Match bank, card and Stripe lines to the ledger, trace each break, reconcile inventory to its valuation report and propose bank rules and fee journals as drafts.

outputs.name: Proposed bank rules and draft fee journals

checks.name: Each reconciled balance equals the statement or report balance, or the gap is itemised
Stripe gross less fees and refunds equals bank deposits for the month, or the gap is itemised
Inventory valuation equals the ledger inventory account, with differences explained
Everything written to Xero is a draft; nothing is posted

stages.name: Build one accrual schedule with draft journals
stages.goal: Move the spreadsheet into one schedule with support, basis and reversal date, and draft the journals, auto-reversing where the entry reverses.

checks.name: Every accrual cites its support and basis
Schedule totals tie to the Xero accrual and prepayment accounts, with any gap documented
Every draft journal balances and states its reversal date
Last month's accruals are checked for reversal and for actual invoices received

stages.name: Build the board pack that ties to the ledger
stages.goal: Draft statements and variance commentary from the reconciled ledger, with every pack number traced to a Xero report.

checks.name: Every figure in the pack is traced to a named Xero report and the difference is zero
Balance sheet balances and cash agrees to the bank reconciliations
Every line beyond the agreed limit has a reason and its evidence
Figures that depend on unposted drafts are marked

stages.name: Finance manager posts approved entries and locks the period
stages.goal: The finance manager posts the approved draft journals one at a time in Xero, switches on each approved bank rule, then sets the lock date. This is where the drafts from reconciliations and accruals are seen. The AI re-ties the pack to the posted ledger.

checks.name: Each entry posted has a recorded approval by the finance manager
After posting, the pack ties to the ledger again and the difference is zero
The lock date is set and read back from Xero
Nothing was posted that was not on the approved list

stages.name: Measure the close against five days
stages.goal: Time the first close on the new calendar and compare it with the baseline and the guardrails.

checks.name: Close days use the same start and end definition as the baseline
Board pack errors found after sign-off and unreconciled differences are counted
One close is reported as a result for that month, not as proof the target is reached

stages.name: Keep what we learned
stages.goal: Record the slowest task of the close, the one root cause to remove next month, and the rules for the calendar and checklist.

checks.name: One root cause is chosen for next month with an owner
Each proposed rule says whether it holds for this close, this business or the playbook

hypotheses.statement: Reconciliation backlog on the bank, card and Stripe accounts sits on the critical path.
hypotheses.test: Count unreconciled lines and oldest dates per account at day 0, and compare with when the reconciliation task finished.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Large or old backlogs exist at day 0 and downstream tasks wait for reconciliation.
hypotheses.refute_if: Accounts are current at day 0 and reconciliation finishes early.

hypotheses.statement: The accruals spreadsheet is late or error-prone and holds up the journals.
hypotheses.test: Compare the last three months of accruals with the invoices that arrived and check whether reversals match.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Accruals are finished late or reversals and actuals disagree.
hypotheses.refute_if: Accruals finish early and reverse cleanly.

hypotheses.statement: Hand reconciliation of the separate inventory system finishes late and leaves differences.
hypotheses.test: Note when inventory was reconciled in the last close and the unexplained gap between valuation and ledger.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Inventory finishes in the last days or leaves unexplained gaps.

hypotheses.statement: Stripe payouts net of fees make the bank reconciliation slow and leave a clearing balance.
hypotheses.test: Compare the Stripe clearing account with the Stripe balance report and bank deposits.
hypotheses.confirm_if: The clearing balance drifts or payouts need manual splitting.

hypotheses.statement: There is no fixed calendar, so inputs arrive late and tasks wait on each other.
hypotheses.test: List who waited on whom in the timings and when inputs were due versus received.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Waiting time is a large share of the 15 days.
hypotheses.refute_if: Tasks run back to back with little waiting.

hypotheses.statement: Review starts after everything is done, so rework stretches the close and lets errors reach the board pack.
hypotheses.test: Count review comments and corrections after the first pack draft and when the review began.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Most corrections are found at the end and trace to earlier tasks.

hypotheses.statement: The board pack is assembled by copying figures, so errors creep in.
hypotheses.test: Trace each line of the last pack to a Xero report and count differences.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Any line cannot be traced or differs.

measurement.window: The first full close run on the new calendar, then the next close to confirm; each close measured from last day of month to sign-off and lock.
measurement.min_volume: At least two closes before any claim that 5 working days is reached; one close is a single result.
measurement.stop_rule: Stop and go back to the approved process for that month if a board pack error is found or anything is posted without approval.
